title: Arriving in Kansas City in spring 1934
summary: After playing Denver, where they followed Bennie Moten's band, the Murphy band reaches Depression-era Kansas City, wide open with crime and jazz.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Cliff, you were saying that going to Kansas City was the biggest thing that happened to you in life just before the phone rang. So you tell me, what year was it that you were in Kansas City?
Going into the Spring of 1934, I think. We had already played --
When you say 'we', who all were you?
Now I'm still with Dan Murphy. I'm just about to break ... we had played in Denver at Elliche's

Gardens -- and we followed a band in there that was called Benny Moten's Orchestra. Now I remember following them in, and I only bring this up because Bennie Moten, shortly after that was operated on, I think, for a tonsil, and had died, and we hit Kansas City and Count Basie had taken a band into the Reno Club -- he took the nucleus of some of Bennie Moten's orchestra.
But I have to put this in perspective. The Depression was heavy around the country, as you know, in '34, still.

Yeah, and the prospects for out of work musicians were bleak -- and we were in the streets of Kansas City. We were there on a Sunday, and I'm getting a little ahead of myself in telling about Basie. I knew little about what was happening there except a cab driver or somebody told me -- I had only a couple of dollars in my pocket -- told me it was Sunday and nothing was opened until Monday, they had the blue laws there -- why I don't know. But crime was rampant along with jazz.
